If you want a non GPU version here's a compact JavaScript thing that I use sometimes.

    const min = Math.min;
    const max = Math.max;
    const median = (a, b, c) => max(min(a, b), min(max(a, b), c));

    const intHash = x => {
      x *= 0xed5ad4bb;
      x ^= x >> 11;
      x = Math.imul(x,0xac4c1b51);
      x ^= x >> 15;
      x = Math.imul(x,0x31848bab);
      x ^= x >> 14;
      return x;
   }

   const makeRandom = seed => {
      let index=0;
      let random = (x=index) => {
        let pattern = intHash( (x + seed) & 0x7fffffff)
        let intValue = intHash( (x + pattern)  & 0x7fffffff);
        index=++x;
        return intValue / 0x7fffffff;
      }
      return random;
    }

    let ss=(v,a=0,b=1,w=v*v*v*(v*(v*6-15)+10))=>(1.0-w)*a+(w*b); 
    let positiveMod=(v,size,q=v%size)=>v<0?size+q:q;
    let clamp = a=> a<0?0:a>1?1:a;
    let perlinRandom = makeRandom(seed);
    let perlin=(x,y,wrapX=256,wrapY=wrapX)=> {    
      let dg=(ix,iy,gi=perlinRandom(positiveMod(iy,wrapY)*wrapX+positiveMod(ix,wrapX)*2)*Math.PI*2)  =>
          ((x-ix)*Math.sin(gi)) + ((y-iy)*Math.cos(gi));
      let u=0|x;
      let v=0|y;
      let sx=x-u; 
      let sy=y-v;
      let u1=(u+1);
      let v1=(v+1);
      return ss(sy,ss(sx,dg(u,v),dg(u1,v)),ss(sx,dg(u,v1),dg(u1,v1)));
    }

    let wrapPerlin=(x,y,wrapX=2,wrapY=wrapX)=>perlin(x*wrapX,y*wrapY,wrapX,wrapY);
It's a bit cryptic because it's used for size coding, ss() is a smoothstep. dg() is apparent enough if you look at any Perlin description. wrapPerlin can be used if you want 0..1 to repeat n times.
